scale_instruction: Enter ONE number from 1 to 5. Every row is worth 5 points; harder sections have more rows and therefore more weight.
guidance: Judge the final Stage 3 work, using the previous-phase requirements as the baseline. Reward evidence, correct integration, and purposeful design - not complexity for its own sake. Testing: look for real trials/results, not only claims. Hardware: reward the best-fit use of components and reliable integration. Teamwork & presentation: look for shared ownership, clear communication, and the ability of multiple members to answer questions.

score_levels.label: Weak
score_levels.description: Missing, incorrect, non-functional, or little/no meaningful evidence.

score_levels.label: Developing
score_levels.description: Partially demonstrated; important gaps remain or substantial support is needed.

score_levels.label: Meets Expectations
score_levels.description: Core requirement is present, understandable, and works at an acceptable/basic level.

score_levels.label: Strong
score_levels.description: Complete, accurate, well integrated, and supported by good evidence; only minor issues.

score_levels.label: Excellent
score_levels.description: Highly effective, reliable, purposeful, well-tested/polished, and clearly justified by the team.

templates.title: Stage 3 Judges' Rubric - DEMI Grade 4
templates.subtitle: App Lab Project - Stage 3 Judge Evaluation

sections.title: Problem, Research & Solution
criteria: Problem & target user
The team clearly defines the real-world problem, who is affected, and why it matters.
Research on similar solutions
Shows credible examples/screenshots of 1-2 similar apps or solutions and explains what was learned.
Research insight / gap
Explains what is missing or could be improved in existing solutions and connects that insight to the project.
App solution & main features
The app purpose and 2-3 main features directly address the identified problem and user needs.

sections.title: UX & Prototype Design
criteria: User flow
Screen-to-screen journey is logical, complete, and easy to follow.
Wireframes / screen design
Screens or mockups match the planned features and show a clear interface structure.
Usability & design consistency
Buttons, labels, navigation, layout, and visual choices are understandable and consistent for the target user.

sections.title: Programming & Functionality
criteria: Working prototype
Core app screens and planned features function during the demonstration.
Events & user input
Events such as button clicks trigger the correct actions and user inputs are handled properly.
Variables & conditions
Variables and conditional logic are used correctly to control app behavior.
Loops / functions / data logic
Uses suitable loops, functions, lists, or reusable logic where needed; logic is organized rather than repeated unnecessarily.
Reliability & correctness
App produces correct results, handles common mistakes reasonably, and does not break during normal use.

sections.title: Testing & Improvement
criteria: Testing coverage
Team tests important screens, buttons, inputs, and user journeys instead of only one happy path.
Evidence of testing
Shows concrete evidence such as test notes, screenshots, user feedback, before/after examples, or repeated trials.
Improvement from findings
Team identifies issues found during testing and explains or demonstrates meaningful improvements.

sections.title: Business & Value
criteria: User value & delivery idea
Explains who benefits, what value the app provides, and a realistic way it could be offered or shared.
Differentiation & feasibility
Explains why the solution is useful compared with alternatives and keeps the idea realistic for the intended users.

sections.title: Teamwork & Presentation
criteria: Shared teamwork & roles
Participation is balanced; team members contribute and can explain their own role in the project.
Clear communication & demo
Presentation is organized, understandable, within time, and the demo supports the story of the project.
Questions & project understanding
Team members answer judge questions clearly and show shared understanding of the app, decisions, and testing.

bonus.title: Extra Requirements / Optional Bonus
criteria: Advanced app feature - usefulness & depth
Optional extra feature meaningfully strengthens the same app rather than adding an unrelated idea.
Advanced app feature - working evidence
Shows screenshots/code or a working demonstration proving the advanced feature is implemented or credibly prototyped.

templates.title: Stage 3 Judges' Rubric - DEMI Grade 5
templates.subtitle: Arduino + AI Project - Stage 3 Judge Evaluation

sections.title: Problem, Research & Solution
criteria: Problem, target user & research
Clearly explains the problem, user, importance, and supporting research about similar ideas or needs.
Solution alignment
The proposed solution and its functions directly address the researched problem.
User value
The team can explain how the final system helps the target user and why the solution is worthwhile.

sections.title: Hardware & System Design
criteria: Purposeful kit/component choice
Hardware is selected because it fits the solution; unnecessary components are avoided and each chosen part has a clear role.
Input/output component use
Sensors and outputs/actuators are used correctly and their roles match the Stage 2 hardware plan.
Circuit correctness & safety
Connections are technically appropriate, organized, and safe for the intended prototype.
System integration
Input -> Arduino/controller -> output behavior works as one coherent system and matches the block/circuit design.
Best use of hardware & reliability
Hardware capabilities are used effectively for the problem, and the physical setup performs consistently during repeated demonstrations.

sections.title: Programming & AI Integration
criteria: Programming logic
Events/inputs, variables, conditions, loops, and outputs work together correctly.
Code organization
Functions or reusable blocks are used appropriately; code is readable and avoids unnecessary repetition.
AI/ML feature relevance
AI feature supports the same problem and is more than a disconnected add-on.
AI evidence & integration
Team shows model/concept evidence and clearly explains how AI input/output connects to the overall solution.

sections.title: Prototype, Testing & Improvement
criteria: Prototype completeness
The physical/digital prototype demonstrates the main planned behavior end-to-end.
Evidence of testing
Shows repeated tests, observations, measurements, screenshots, logs, or other evidence rather than only stating that testing happened.
Improvement & reliability
Team uses test findings to improve timing, thresholds, interaction, accuracy, or reliability and can explain the change.

sections.title: Business & Value
criteria: Customer & value proposition
Target customer/user matches the original problem and the value is clear.
Practical delivery / feasibility
Explains a realistic way the solution could be offered, used, or adopted.

sections.title: Teamwork & Presentation
criteria: Shared teamwork & contribution
Roles are balanced and all members visibly contribute to building, testing, or explaining the project.
Technical communication
Team explains hardware, code, AI, and design decisions in language appropriate to judges.
Presentation, demo & Q&A
Presentation is clear and well paced; demo evidence is convincing; answers show shared understanding.

bonus.title: Extra Requirements / Optional Bonus
criteria: Advanced programming feature
Optional stronger programming feature (functions, lists, nested logic, etc.) is useful and supported by code/logic evidence.
Advanced AI feature
Optional AI feature goes beyond the basic AI requirement and is supported by a model, screenshot, result, or credible prototype evidence.

templates.title: Stage 3 Judges' Rubric - DECI Level 1
templates.subtitle: MIT App Inventor + Kit Project - Stage 3 Judge Evaluation

sections.title: Problem, Research & Solution
criteria: Problem, target users & research
Clearly defines the problem, exact users, importance, and supporting research findings/sources.
Solution & user interaction
Solution directly addresses the problem and explains how users will interact with it step by step.
Main features & value
3-4 main functions are purposeful and connected to the original user need.

sections.title: System, Circuit & Kit Use
criteria: System structure
Overall system/block flow is clear: trigger/input -> controller/processing -> output/action.
Purposeful kit & component choice
Car/Robot Arm Kit and specific components are chosen because they fit the project, not simply because they are available.
Circuit/component understanding
Connections and component roles are technically reasonable and match the design.
Best hardware use & integration
Hardware capabilities are used effectively and, where implemented, behave reliably as part of the same solution.

sections.title: Programming Logic
criteria: Events / inputs
Program begins from clear user/system events or inputs and reacts correctly.
Conditions & decisions
Decision logic matches the intended behavior and important cases.
Loops / timing / repeated behavior
Repeated actions or waiting/timing logic are handled correctly where required.
Outputs & logic consistency
Program outputs match the flowchart/blocks and the described system behavior.

sections.title: MIT App Inventor & User Experience
criteria: App role & user flow
App clearly supports or controls the solution and users can navigate the intended flow.
Screens / interface quality
Screens are understandable, consistent, and appropriate for the target users.
Blocks & working evidence
Real blocks/screens or a working demo show that the planned app logic is implemented.

sections.title: Testing & Integration
criteria: End-to-end testing evidence
Team shows that the app and any hardware interaction were tested through realistic use cases, not only isolated parts.
Reliability & improvement
Team identifies failures/limitations and explains changes or next improvements based on testing.

sections.title: Business & Value
criteria: Benefit & delivery model
Explains who benefits, the value provided, and a realistic way the solution could reach users.

sections.title: Teamwork & Presentation
criteria: Shared contribution
All team members participate and can explain the part they contributed.
Communication & demonstration
Presentation is clear and the live/demo evidence supports the project story.
Q&A & shared understanding
Team answers questions accurately and shows shared understanding of app, hardware, logic, and user need.

bonus.title: Extra Requirements / Optional Bonus
criteria: AI feature
Optional AI/ML/computer vision/NLP feature strengthens the same solution and includes prototype/evidence.
Advanced App Inventor feature
Optional advanced app feature (e.g., multiple screens, data storage, enhanced interaction) is useful and supported by working evidence.

templates.title: Stage 3 Judges' Rubric - DECI Level 2
templates.subtitle: Arduino + Web Integration Project - Stage 3 Judge Evaluation

sections.title: Problem, Research & Solution
criteria: Problem, users & research
Defines a real problem and target users with relevant research findings/references.
Solution fit & user interaction
Solution directly addresses the problem and clearly explains how users interact with it.
Features & value
Main functions are purposeful, coherent, and create a clear advantage or value for the user.

sections.title: System, Circuit, Hardware & Kit
criteria: System data flow
Full path from sensor/input -> Arduino processing -> communication/output -> web/software is clear and correct.
Purposeful kit selection
Car/Robot Arm Kit choice is justified by the components actually needed; unnecessary kit parts are not forced into the project.
Component roles
Arduino, sensors, actuators, communication modules, and other parts each have a clear and correct role.
Circuit correctness
Power, ground, signal, TX/RX, and other relevant connections are technically reasonable and match the prototype.
Best hardware use & reliability
Hardware is used effectively for the problem and performs consistently in repeated trials/demos.

sections.title: Programming & Control Logic
criteria: Inputs, conditions & outputs
Sensor/input readings drive correct decisions and outputs.
Loops & functions
Repeated behavior and reusable functions/blocks are used appropriately and clearly.
Control reliability
Program behavior is stable, understandable, and consistent with the flowchart/pseudocode.

sections.title: Web Interface Integration
criteria: Web role & system connection
Web interface displays/controls the exact information produced by the system and has a clear purpose.
UI quality & usability
Interface is readable, organized, and appropriate for the target users.
Working integration evidence
Screenshots/demo show that the web interface and hardware/data flow are credibly connected or implemented.

sections.title: Testing & Hardware Evidence
criteria: Evidence of testing
Shows repeated hardware/software tests, measurements, logs, screenshots, or scenario results.
Improvement & robustness
Team uses findings to improve thresholds, communication, UI, wiring, reliability, or error handling.

sections.title: Business & Value
criteria: Customer, alternatives & value
Identifies customer, existing alternatives/competitors, and explains practical value/differentiation.

sections.title: Teamwork & Presentation
criteria: Shared contribution & roles
Team members visibly contribute across hardware, code, web, testing, or documentation.
Technical communication
Explains system flow and design decisions clearly without relying on one member for all technical answers.
Presentation, demo & Q&A
Presentation is clear, well paced, evidence-based, and questions are answered confidently.

bonus.title: Extra Requirements / Optional Bonus
criteria: AI / data feature
Optional AI, ML, or data-analysis feature uses relevant project data and includes a useful result or visualization.
Advanced system feature
Optional cybersecurity, automation, IoT, or software enhancement strengthens the existing system and includes evidence.

templates.title: Stage 3 Judges' Rubric - DECI Level 3
templates.subtitle: ESP32 + Track Integration Project - Stage 3 Judge Evaluation

sections.title: Problem, Research & Solution
criteria: Problem, user & research
Clearly defines the problem/user and supports it with relevant research findings and references.
Solution & user interaction
Solution directly addresses the problem and explains a complete user interaction.
Features & value
Main functions are coherent, useful, and consistent with the same target user.

sections.title: System, Hardware, IoT & Circuit
criteria: ESP32 system architecture
System clearly explains sensor/input -> ESP32 processing -> decision -> output/communication, including relevant ESP32 capabilities.
Purposeful platform & component choice
Kit/platform, ESP32/ESP32 Camera, sensors, and actuators are selected because they fit the project.
IoT communication
Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/data flow is technically sensible, including two-way communication where needed.
Circuit correctness
Circuit connections and selected GPIO/input types are reasonable and match the implemented plan.
Best hardware use & reliability
Hardware/ESP32 capabilities are used effectively and operate consistently under repeated demonstrations.

sections.title: Programming & AI / Data
criteria: Programming/control logic
Inputs, decisions, timing/loops, outputs, and communication are implemented logically and reliably.
Data collection & decisions
Collected sensor/image data is relevant and is used appropriately to drive decisions or actions.
AI approach & relevance
If AI/computer vision is used, classification/object detection or other approach fits the problem and data.
Evidence of AI/data flow
Shows model/data-flow/visual evidence and explains how results connect back to the system.

sections.title: Digital Identity & Track Integration
criteria: Digital identity
Project name, logo, palette, and visual style are consistent and fit the product/user.
Applied track integration
Relevant team track output (Web, UI/UX, Data Science, Cybersecurity) is clearly connected to the same ESP32 project and shows real evidence.

sections.title: Testing & Validation
criteria: Testing evidence & success checks
Shows repeated functional tests or data/communication tests with observable success criteria.
Improvement & system reliability
Team identifies weaknesses and improves hardware, logic, data, interface, or communication based on evidence.

sections.title: Business & Value
criteria: Customer, value & pricing
Target customer, value proposition, and basic pricing/delivery idea are clear and realistic.

sections.title: Teamwork & Presentation
criteria: Cross-track teamwork
Members integrate their track contributions into one solution instead of presenting disconnected pieces.
Communication & technical ownership
Different members can explain decisions and demonstrate understanding beyond only their own slide/part.
Presentation, demo & Q&A
Project story is clear and professional; evidence is well selected; team handles judge questions effectively.

bonus.title: Extra Requirements / Optional Bonus
criteria: Advanced AI feature
Optional advanced AI/ML feature goes beyond the core data plan and includes prototype/evidence.
Advanced system feature
Optional stronger IoT, cybersecurity, data processing, or digital experience feature improves the same system and includes evidence.

templates.title: Stage 3 Judges' Rubric - DECI Levels 4 & 5
templates.subtitle: Combined Advanced Project - Stage 3 Judge Evaluation

sections.title: Problem Analysis & Complete Solution
criteria: Problem, research & opportunity
Defines the real problem, target users, existing alternatives, supporting research, and the specific value/opportunity for the solution.
Complete end-to-end solution
User journey and system behavior form a complete flow from data capture/input through processing, user action, and feedback/logging where appropriate.

sections.title: Architecture, Hardware & Embedded IoT
criteria: System architecture & data flow
Hardware, ESP32/ESP32 Camera, communication, AI/software processing, and user interface are connected in a technically coherent architecture.
Purposeful hardware selection
Physical platform, sensors/actuators, ESP32, and ESP32 Camera roles are justified by the problem; components are not added without purpose.
Circuit & embedded logic
Circuit, input processing, states/events, actuator responses, and control logic are technically sound and match the implementation.
IoT / communication integration
Data transmission, cloud/local processing, and device-to-system communication are reliable and appropriate for the use case.
Best hardware use, reliability & scalability
Hardware capabilities are used efficiently; system performs consistently and design choices consider reliability and practical scaling.

sections.title: AI, Data Processing & Data Science
criteria: Data pipeline
Data collection, preparation, processing, and decision flow are clear and technically appropriate.
AI/ML approach & performance evidence
Chosen AI/ML method fits the task; team shows relevant outputs, confidence/accuracy evidence, or justified evaluation.
Data science insight
Collected project data is organized/visualized to produce a useful insight that supports a real user or business decision.
Integration of AI/data into system behavior
AI/data results trigger meaningful dashboard updates, alerts, predictions, recommendations, or other actions in the same solution.

sections.title: Product, UX, Web & Cybersecurity
criteria: Product identity & professional visualization
Brand/UI is consistent and polished; mixed Level 4-5 team includes strong product visuals/digital assets appropriate to Level 5 depth.
Web application integration
Web/app interface exposes the correct live/history/control information from the hardware/AI system and supports the intended user flow.
Cybersecurity design
Authentication/authorization, access control, communication/data protection, and relevant risks are addressed in a way that fits the architecture.

sections.title: Business, Testing & Improvement
criteria: Business model & product planning
Customer, value proposition, pricing, competitors/alternatives, and delivery approach are complete and realistic.
Testing evidence & measurable success criteria
Team tests under relevant conditions and shows evidence such as logs, accuracy results, repeated runs, failure cases, or comparison to ground truth.
Iteration, reliability & improvement
Test results lead to concrete improvements; team can explain limitations, reliability concerns, and next technical/product steps.

sections.title: Teamwork & Presentation
criteria: Cross-discipline teamwork & ownership
Hardware, software, AI/data, design, security, and business work are integrated; members have visible contributions and shared ownership.
Technical communication & decision justification
Team explains architecture and tradeoffs clearly and can justify why technologies/components were chosen.
Presentation, live demo & Q&A
Presentation is polished and concise, demo evidence is convincing, and multiple members answer judge questions confidently.

bonus.title: Extra Requirements / Optional Bonus
criteria: Advanced AI/ML feature
Optional advanced AI feature goes beyond the core AI/data pipeline and is supported by evidence or a credible prototype.
Advanced IoT / security feature
Optional advanced cloud, real-time communication, automation, monitoring, or security capability strengthens the same architecture.
Level 5 advanced security / reliability
Optional Level-5-depth feature such as stronger authentication, secure protocols, monitoring, risk management, or reliability safeguards is demonstrated with evidence.
